Rashi on Ketubot 12a:11:1.english: If we say [it is] concerning the first clause - Concerning the custom that they seclude [the couple].

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:11:2.english: Anyone who conducted [himself] to be secluded [with her] is what it needed to say - That he cannot make a claim [concerning virginity].

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:12:1.english: Rather, concerning the latter clause - [Referring] to the custom of examination by the groomsmen.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:12:2.hebrew: כל שלא מושמש מיבעי ליה - דהטוען טענת בתולים הוא הבעל, והוא אינו נוהג מישמוש שבו [שאינו תלוי בבעל], אלא על אבי הכלה למשמשו שלא יאבד את בתוליה, ומשמוש בכלה שלא תביא דם מן החוץ תלוי בבעל. והיכי תני: "כל בעל שלא נהג מישמוש אינו יכול לטעון טענת בתולים"? כ"ש דאם לא נהג למשמש, והם מישמשו אותו, דיכול לטעון! הכי איבעי ליה למתני: "כל שלא מושמש אינו יכול לטעון", דשמא ראה ואבד:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:12:2.english: "Anyone who was not examined" is what it needed [to say] - For the one who makes a claim of non-virginity is the husband, and he does not conduct the examination of himself [for it is not dependent on the husband]; rather, it is upon the father of the bride to examine him so that he does not destroy her tokens of virginity, whereas the examination of the bride—so that she does not bring blood from outside—is dependent on the husband. How then can it teach, "Any [husband] who did not practice examination cannot make a claim of non-virginity"? All the more so, if he did not practice examining [her], while they examined him, he can make a claim! Thus it should have taught: "Anyone who was not examined cannot make a claim," for perhaps he saw [the tokens of virginity] and destroyed [them].

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:13:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - האי "כל שלא נהג" אמנהג דגליל קאי, דתנא בברייתא: "ובגליל לא היו עושין כן", ועלה קאי: כל שלא נהג כמנהג הזה בגליל, אלא נתייחד כמנהג שביהודה, אינו יכול לטעון:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:13:1.english: Rather, Rava said - This [statement], "Anyone who did not practice," refers to the custom of the Galilee, for it was taught in the baraita: "And in the Galilee they would not do so," and it refers to that: anyone who did not practice this custom in the Galilee, but rather secluded himself [with his bride] according to the custom in Judea, cannot make a [virginity] claim.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:14:1.english: A widow of priests - A widow [who is] the daughter of a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:14:2.hebrew: היו גובין לבתולה - בת כהן כשנישאת לכהן, וכ"ש כשנישאת לישראל:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:14:2.english: They would collect for a virgin - [Referring to] a priest's daughter when she marries a priest, and all the more so when she marries an Israelite.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:16:1.english: There were two ordinances - For a widow, the daughter of a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:1:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת כו' - דהא ודאי בחזקת בתולה כנסה, דסמך אעדים, וקאמר אין יכול להפסידה מנה הראוי לאלמנה מן הנישואין:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:1:1.english: That is to say, etc. - For he certainly married her with the presumption [that she was] a virgin, since he relied on witnesses, and [yet Rabbah] says [that] he cannot deprive her of the maneh that is due to a widow from marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:2:1.hebrew: וניחוש שמא תחתיו זינתה - אמתניתין פריך, דקתני: "אין השני יכול לטעון טענת בתולים", ולא מזקיקינן ליה לבא לבית דין, ולא יתברר הדבר אם תחתיו זינתה אם לא, ושמא אסורה היא לו. בשלמא אהנך דלעיל, דאמרן: "כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה יש לה כתובה", לא מקשינן, דאיכא למימר כשבא לבית דין ובאו עדים שזינתה קודם לכן; אבל הכא קתני "אין יכול לטעון", מתוך כך לא יבא לב"ד:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:2:1.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps she committed adultery while under him - [The Gemara] is asking on the Mishnah, which teaches: "The second [husband] cannot make a virginity claim," and we do not require him to come to court, and [thus] the matter will not be clarified whether she committed adultery while under him or not, and perhaps she is forbidden to him. Granted, regarding those [cases] above, where it stated: "[If] he married her on the presumption that she was a virgin and she was found to have had intercourse, she has a ketubah," we did not raise [this] difficulty, since it is possible to say [that refers to] when he came to court and witnesses came [and testified] that she committed adultery prior to that; however, here it teaches "he cannot make a claim," [and] as a result he will not come to court.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:2:2.hebrew: כשקידש ובעל לאלתר גרסינן, ולא גרסינן כשקידש לאלתר ובעל לאלתר. שלא פירש ממנה בין קידושין לבעילה, דודאי לא תחתיו זינתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:2:2.english: We read [the text as] "when he betrothed and engaged in intercourse immediately," and we do not read "when he betrothed immediately and engaged in intercourse immediately." [That is,] he did not separate from her between betrothal and intercourse, so she certainly did not commit adultery while under him.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:3:1.hebrew: ואיכא דמתני לה - להא דרבה ורב אשי ורב שרביא אמתני':
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:3:1.english: And there are those who teach it - This [statement] of Rabbah, Rav Ashi, and Rav Sheravya, [they teach] regarding the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:4:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת - מדקתני מתני', אין להן טענת בתולים:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:4:1.english: That is to say - From [the fact] that the Mishnah teaches: "They do not have a claim of virginity."

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:5:1.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps she committed adultery while under him - And why does [the baraita] teach [that] they do not have a claim of virginity?

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:1.english: The one who taught it - [Referring] to this [exchange] of Rabbah and Rav Ashi, with regard to the baraita.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:2.hebrew: כ"ש אמתני' - דכיון דאברייתא, אע"ג דאמרו עדים לא נסתרה לראשון, ושני זה בחזקת בתולה כנסה, ואפילו הכי אהדר ליה רב אשי לרבה: לעולם לא תשמע כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה יש לה כתובה, דשאני הכא שהרי כנסה ראשון — כל שכן אמתניתין, דלא הבטיחוהו עדים על כך, איכא למתנייה לדרבה ומאי דאהדר ליה רב אשי:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:2.english: All the more so with regard to our Mishnah - For since with regard to the baraita, even though witnesses said she was not secluded with the first [husband], and this second [husband] married her with the presumption of [her being] a virgin, and even so Rav Ashi replied to Rabbah: "Still, do not infer [that if] one married her with the presumption of [her being] a virgin and she was found to be non-virgin, she has a ketubah, for here it is different since the first [husband] married her" — all the more so with regard to our Mishnah, where witnesses did not assure him of this, can one teach [the statement] of Rabbah and what Rav Ashi replied to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:3.english: And the one who teaches it - [That] of Rabbah and Rav Ashi, with regard to the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:4.hebrew: אבל אברייתא לא - מתני להו, דמברייתא ודאי שפיר ש"מ "זאת אומרת" דרבה, ועלה לא הוה לרב אשי לאהדורי: "שאני הכא שהרי כנסה ראשון", דמצי אמר: "אנא אעדים סמכי". וכיון דקתני: "אין השני יכול לטעון טענת בתולים", שמעינן ודאי דזאת אומרת: "כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה — יש לה כתובה":
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:6:4.english: However, with regard to the baraita, not - He teaches them [with regard to the Mishnah], for from the baraita one certainly derives well the "that is to say" [statement] of Rabbah, and regarding it Rav Ashi could not have replied, "Here it is different, for the first [husband] married her," since [the second husband] can say, "I relied on witnesses." And since [the baraita] teaches, "The second [husband] cannot make a claim of non-virginity," we certainly learn that this is to say: [If] one married her under the presumption [that she was] a virgin and she was found [to be] a non-virgin, she has a ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:8:1.hebrew: מקומות מקומות יש - שחלוקין במנהגם, ונפקא מינה דהיכא דלא נהיגי לייחד, יכול לטעון:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:8:1.english: There are [different] places - That differ in their custom, and the practical difference is that where they are not accustomed to seclude [the bride and groom], he can make a claim [of non-virginity].

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:8:2.english: As it is taught - That there are [different] places.

Rashi on Ketubot 12a:9:1.hebrew: למשמש - לפשפש ולמשמש במעשיהן באותו הלילה, שלא יקלקלו זה את זה במעשיהם בתרמית: שלא יראה זה דם בתולים ויאבד, וזו לא תביא מפה שיש עליה טיפי דמים. ובמקום שנהגו למשמש, לא נהגו לייחד; דאילו במקום שנהגו לייחד, מאי מישמוש בעי? הרי אין שם טענת בתולים. אלמא, ביהודה מקומות מקומות יש:
Rashi on Ketubot 12a:9:1.english: To examine - To search and examine their actions on that night, so that they should not ruin [things for] one another through their actions with deception: so that he [the groom] should not see virginity blood and destroy [it], and she [the bride] should not bring a cloth that has drops of blood upon it. And in a place where they were accustomed to examine [the couple], they were not accustomed to seclude [them together before marriage]; for in a place where they were accustomed to seclude [them], what examination is needed? Behold, there is no claim of [non-]virginity there. Thus, in Judea there are [different] places [with different customs].

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:14:1.hebrew: בית דין של כהנים היו גובין כו' ולא מיחו בידם חכמים - אע"פ שלא כתב בלשון תוספת, אלא "ארבע מאות דחזו ליכי", וקא ס"ד דלא תגבה, דלא חזו ובלשון תוספת לא כתב — קא משמע לן דמנהג טוב מאד הוא, וראוי להיות בכהונה ובמשפחות המיוחסות, ושייך בהו למימר "דחזו ליכי". ואפי' לא כתב לה כתובה, גובה ארבע מאות בתנאי ב"ד, כמו בבנות ישראל מאתים, דתקנה גמורה היא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:14:1.english: A court of priests would collect, etc., and the Sages did not reprimand them - Even though [the husband] did not write [it] in the language of an addition, but rather [wrote], "Four hundred [zuz] that are fitting for you," and one might have thought that she would not collect [it], since they are not fitting [for her] and he did not write [it] in the language of an addition — [the Mishnah] teaches us that it is a very good custom, and it is proper for it to be [practiced] among the priesthood and among distinguished families, and it is applicable to them to say, "that are fitting for you." And even if he did not write a marriage contract for her, she collects four hundred [zuz] as a stipulation of the court, just as [with] Israelite women [who collect] two hundred [zuz], for it is a full-fledged enactment.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:16:1.hebrew: שתי תקנות הוו - וליכא למימר דחדא תקנה הואי, ומתני' קודם תקנה וברייתא לאחר תקנה שתיקנו לאלמנה מאתים — דהא חזינן השתא דלית להו מאתים. וליכא למימר נמי דמעיקרא כי תקינו לבתולה ארבע מאות, תקינו גם כן לאלמנה מאתים, דאין סברא לתקן לאלמנה מאתים אם לא אחר שראו צורך דמזלזלי בהו. [הילכך מעיקרא לא רצו לשנותה משאר אלמנה, וכיון דחזו דקא מזלזלי בהו, ראו שהיה צורך — תקון להם מאתן, וכיון דחזו דפרשי מינייהו, אהדרינהו למילתייהו.] ולכך הוצרך לומר שתי תקנות הוו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:16:1.english: There were two ordinances - And one cannot say that there was [only] one ordinance, and [that] the Mishnah was [taught] before the ordinance and the baraita after the ordinance when they instituted two hundred [zuz] for a widow — for we see now that they do not have two hundred [zuz]. And one also cannot say that initially, when they instituted four hundred [zuz] for a virgin, they also instituted two hundred [zuz] for a widow, for there is no logical reason to institute two hundred [zuz] for a widow unless [it was] after they saw a need [for it], because [people] were treating them lightly. [Therefore, initially they did not want to differentiate her from any other widow; and once they saw that [people] were treating them lightly, they saw that there was a need — they instituted two hundred [zuz] for them; and once they saw that [people] were abstaining from [marrying] them, they restored them to their [original] status.] And therefore, [Rav Ashi] needed to say that there were two ordinances.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:1.hebrew: אמר רבה זאת אומרת - נראה דהכא גרסינן רבה, דהא רבא קאמר לעיל דמקח טעות לגמרי משמע. ואי גרסינן הכא רבא, א"כ תיקשי מתניתין רישא לסיפא, דהא "זאת אומרת" איכא למידק נמי ממתניתין כדאמרינן בסמוך; אלא ודאי נראה דהכא גרס רבה, דרבא — דאמר לעיל מקח טעות לגמרי משמע — יפרש כמו רב אשי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:1.english: Rabbah said: That is to say - It appears that here we read "Rabbah," for Rava said above that "a mistaken transaction" implies [that it is] completely [void]. And if we read "Rava" here, then the Mishnah would contradict itself from the first clause to the latter clause, since this [inference of] "That is to say" can also be deduced from the Mishnah, as [the Gemara] says shortly. Rather, it certainly appears that here [the text] reads "Rabbah," for Rava — who said above that "a mistaken transaction" implies [that it is] completely [void] — will explain [it] like Rav Ashi.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:2.hebrew: כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה יש לה מנה - והא דקתני "שהרי כנסה ראשון", פירש ריב"ם דהכי משמע ליה: אין לשני טענת בתולין לחסרה מכתובתה כלום, שהרי כנסה ראשון וגרם להיות כתובתה מנה, ואינו יכול לחסרה כלום מאותה מנה, דלא מהניא טענת בתולין אלא ממנה דבתולין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:2.english: "If one married her with the presumptive status of a virgin and she was found [to be] a non-virgin, she has [a marriage contract of] a maneh" - And as for that which it teaches, "because the first [husband] married her," Rivam explained that this is what it means to him: the second [husband] has no virginity claim to deduct anything from her marriage contract, because the first [husband] married her and caused her marriage contract to be a maneh, and he cannot deduct anything from that maneh, for a virginity claim is effective only against the maneh of virginity [the additional maneh given to a virgin].

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:3.hebrew: שאני הכא שהרי כנסה ראשון - ואדעתא דבעולה נישאת; ואע"ג דעדים מעידים שלא נבעלה, אינו סומך על זה מאחר שהיו נישואין, וסבר דלשבחה אומרים כן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:1:3.english: "Here it is different, because the first [husband] brought her in" - And she is married on the assumption [that she is] a non-virgin; and even though witnesses testify that she did not engage in intercourse, he does not rely on this since there was a [prior] marriage, and he thinks that they say so to praise her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:2:1.hebrew: וניחוש שמא תחתיו זינתה - אין לומר דפריך אמאי אינו יכול לטעון טענת בתולים לאוסרה עליו, ניחוש באשת כהן שמא תחתיו זינתה, דליכא אלא חדא ספיקא: ספק תחתיו ספק אין תחתיו. דהא מצי לשנויי דהא דאינו יכול לטעון היינו להפסידה מכתובתה, דאיכא ספק ספיקא, דאפי' תחתיו אימור באונס הוה. ואין זה דוחק, דלעיל נמי מפרש "אינו יכול לטעון טענת בתולים" הכי, דקאמר: למאי? אי לאוסרה עליו, ביהודה אמאי לא כו'! אלא אכתובה פריך, אמאי אינו מפסיד לה. ונראה לר"י דלרב אשי פריך: כיון דבעלמא אית ליה דאין לה כלום, והכא יש לה לפי שכנסה ראשון, א"כ יבא לידי איסור; שזה האיש סבור: כיון שזו יש לה אע"ג דבעלמא לית לה, אם כן מחזקינן אותה ודאי בעולה מבעל ראשון, ואדעת כן רוצים לומר שנשאתי, ובחנם אטרח לבית דין, שודאי לא יאסרוה עלי. ולכך היה לנו להפסיד כתובתה, שיבא לב"ד ולא יטעה לומר שמותרת לו. ואפי' באשת ישראל יש לנו להפסידה, גזירה שיראה כהן שזו לא תאבד כתובתה ויסבור אף בשלו כן, ולא יבא לב"ד. אבל לרבה לא פריך מידי: כיון דבעלמא נמי יש לה, ליכא למיטעי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:2:1.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps she committed adultery while under him - One cannot say that [the Gemara] is asking: "Why can he not make a claim of non-virginity to forbid her to him—let us be concerned in the case of a kohen's wife that perhaps she committed adultery while under him, where there is only a single doubt: perhaps [it occurred] under him, [and] perhaps not under him?" For [if that were the question, Rav Sherevya] could have answered that [the ruling] that he cannot make a claim refers [only] to causing her to forfeit her ketubah, where there is a double doubt, since even [if it occurred] under him, say it was by rape. And this is not a forced [explanation], for earlier as well [the Gemara] explains "he cannot make a claim of non-virginity" in this way, where it says: "For what [purpose]? If to forbid her to him, in Judea why not, etc.!" Rather, [the Gemara here] is asking regarding the ketubah: why does he not cause her to forfeit [it]? And it appears to Ri that [the Gemara] is asking according to Rav Ashi: Since in general he holds that she receives nothing, whereas here she receives [a ketubah] because the first [husband] brought her into [his house], if so, [this] will lead to a prohibition; for this man [the second husband] will think: "Since this [woman] receives [a ketubah] even though in general [such a woman] receives nothing, if so, we presume her to have definitely had intercourse with the first husband, and it is on that assumption that they mean [to say] I married [her], and I would trouble [myself to go] to the court in vain, for they will certainly not forbid her to me." And therefore we ought to cause her to forfeit her ketubah, so that he will come to the court and not err by saying that she is permitted to him. And even in the case of an Israelite's wife we ought to cause her to forfeit [it], [as] a decree [lest] a kohen see that this [woman] does not lose her ketubah and think [the law is] the same for his [wife] as well, and not come to the court. But according to Rabbah [the Gemara] has no difficulty at all: since in general as well she receives [a ketubah], there is no [reason] to err.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:2:2.hebrew: כגון שקידש ובעל לאלתר - וכן צריך נמי להעמיד שהראשון אחר שקידש כנסה לאלתר ומת מיד, ועדים מעידים שלא זינתה תחתיו; דאם נבעלה תחת הראשון, הרי נבעלה לפסול לה ואסורה לכהונה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12a:2:2.english: Where he betrothed [her] and engaged in intercourse immediately - And similarly, it is also necessary to establish that the first [husband], after he betrothed [her], married her immediately and died right away, and [that] witnesses testify that she did not commit adultery while under him; for if she engaged in intercourse [with another] while under the first [husband], she has thereby engaged in intercourse with one disqualified to her and is forbidden to the priesthood.
